notes:
Account: large marketplace with global traffic spikes (US+EU peak). Interested in Redwood Dedicated for predictable cost and strong isolation. Key asks: throughput guarantees for peak shopping events, strict latency SLOs for chat/personalization, and architecture for noisy-neighbor mitigation.

From AE demo (Elena): - They run realtime personalization model (seq length ~512) for ranking and short chat (turns <50 tokens) for support widget. Expect bursty traffic: 700-900 reqs/sec at peak; sustained 60M tokens/day.
Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs, and EU data residency for subset of customers.

Dedicated capacity ask: initial reserved pool sizing guidance: prefer H100 class for low-latency chat; engineering asked for cost/latency tradeoffs between 8xA100-80GB vs 4xH100 nodes. Wants a plan for autoscale bursts (burst reserve or cross-tenant overflow).

Traffic shaping & priority lanes discussion (core): - Need per-route quotas: production chat lane (priority), personalization/ranking lane (medium), ingestion/bulk embeddings (low). - Weighted priority lanes, with preemptible low-priority workers for batch ingestion to avoid impacting P95 chat. - Tenant isolation: prefer pinned GPU pools for high-tier customers + fair-share cgroups for remaining tenants. - Noisy neighbor controls: token/sec throttles, per-tenant circuit breakers, backpressure signals to client, automatic fallback to cheaper model variant when overload. - Per-route SLOs: p95 <120ms for chat; p95 <250ms for ranking; embeddings throughput minimal 40k tokens/s in bulk windows.

SLA negotiation notes: they expect 99.95% uptime for Dedicated control and 99.9% for inference plane; request credits for latency SLO misses and clause for capacity failure during peak events. Procurement pushes for a 12-month reserved contract with quarterly review.

AE/SE action items: 1) draft capacity plan with model profile + GPU sizing (Marco). 2) Add traffic shaping appendix to SOW with concrete per-route quotas and enforcement semantics (Elena). 3) Security to run SOC2 + KMS integration checklist (Priya).

Quoted from engineering lead: "We cannot have noisy bulk embedding jobs bring down chat during flash sales — need hard isolation or preemptible lanes with graceful fallback."
